errors.english: It is explained by the phrase "because of the result."
errors.why: The lemma cited from the root text is simply 'because' (gang gis phyir); 'the result' belongs to the following gloss, not the quoted word.

note: The Sāṃkhya argument (Pradhāna hollow if its manifest results are hollow) is followed correctly; a few lemma citations and the sentence about 'life itself' are shaky.

errors.english: When it has merely begun, it is not the case that it is not the act itself.
errors.why: sbyor ba here is prayoga, the preparatory act: at mere commencement it is not that there is no preparatory act, not 'the act itself'.

fix.find: it is not the case that it is not the act itself.
fix.replace: it is not the case that there is no preparatory act (prayoga).

errors.english: If one subdues the Mara demon of passions and practices restraint, what downfall could there be? It was said to be a "grave fault."
errors.why: This is the standard Vinaya question-and-answer 'If he does X and withholds, what offence is it? A sthūlātyaya'; the rhetorical 'what downfall could there be?' implies no offence, and the 'Māra' reading of bdud 'joms is out of place for a physical act.
In this Mūlasarvāstivāda text the class is the Sanskrit saṅghāvaśeṣa, not the Pali saṅghādisesa.

note: The overall sense of the first saṅghāvaśeṣa commentary comes through, but its technical analysis (prayoga, the offence Q&A) is misread in places.

errors.english: For someone born from the karma of mantras and medicines
errors.why: What is 'produced by the operation of mantra and medicine' is the magical power used to carry the goods, not a person born from it.

note: The toll-evasion casuistry is mostly rendered correctly; some clauses in the miraculous-power passage are garbled, as is the Tibetan.

errors.english: That [note: the ultimate nature] is not of the same category as those [note: ordinary perceptions].
errors.why: The verse says those beings are not knowers of reality (the commentary goes on: only the Buddha knows reality); the same misreading recurs in 'are not fit for that reality'.

fix.find: That [note: the ultimate nature] is not of the same category as those [note: ordinary perceptions].
fix.replace: They are not knowers of reality.

errors.english: regarding the meaning of reality which possesses equanimity [note: original: "upeksha"], characterized as being free from definitions: those who are the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
errors.why: It is the Buddhas who are indifferent to (who disregard) the meaning of reality, which is free from characteristics; reality does not 'possess equanimity'.

fix.find: regarding the meaning of reality which possesses equanimity [note: original: "upeksha"], characterized as being free from definitions: those who are the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
fix.replace: the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are indifferent to the meaning of reality, which is free from characteristics,

errors.english: [note: a steady, unblinking, and panoramic way of looking]
errors.why: The elephant's look (gajanimīlikā) is the elephant's half-closed eyes, i.e. feigning not to see, which is exactly what the passage goes on to say.

fix.find: [note: a steady, unblinking, and panoramic way of looking]
fix.replace: [note: gajanimīlikā, the elephant's half-closed eyes, i.e. feigning not to see]

errors.english: just like a person who is desired [note: one who is sought after or conceptualized]
errors.why: mngon par 'dod pa here means 'the person [the opponent] accepts or posits', not one who is desired.

note: The argument about the Buddha's conventional teaching despite seeing non-duality is recognisable, but the key verse terms (knowers of reality, indifference, the elephant's look) are misread.

errors.english: When the words reached their conclusion
errors.why: The gods' acclamation ('Well done, king!') spread to the ends of the directions; 'reached their conclusion' loses the 'directions' (phyogs mthar).

note: A good verse rendering of the Tibetan (the Sanskrit lines are left untranslated, which is appropriate); one opening phrase is misread.

errors.why: The line finishes 'illuminating the special excellence of [giving]' (sbyin-pa from the previous side); 'for the benefit of others' is not in the text.

errors.english: is born into the world of the Sugata One Gone to Bliss
errors.why: The Sanskrit prakaṭitasugatiḥ means a jewel of a man who shows the good path or destiny is born into the world; it is not 'the world of the Sugata'.

note: The colophon and the opening of the next avadāna are mostly sound; two phrases in the verse are misconstrued.

errors.english: that which has parts is not without cause
errors.why: The Tibetan says that because there is no cause, it is not a whole possessing parts.

fix.find: that which has parts is not without cause
fix.replace: since there is no cause, it is not a whole possessing parts

errors.english: Destruction is not brought about by another agent but occurs due to the inherent nature of things.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the thing perishes by its own nature without producing (ārambha) another entity; it says nothing about destruction not being caused by another agent.

errors.english: If they did, it would lead to the absurdity
errors.why: The absurdity (no difference between contacting and non-contacting atoms) is given as the reason why non-contacting atoms cannot produce a whole; the condition is not 'if they did'.

note: A difficult atomism passage; the general line is followed, but several inferential links are inverted or misattached.

errors.why: In this Mūlasarvāstivāda text the term should be the Sanskrit saṅghāvaśeṣa, not the Pali saṅghādisesa.
This means he should have the text thoroughly settled (fluent and fixed in memory), not that he should be personally composed.

note: The five modes of recitation and the duties of the reciter and elder are rendered accurately, apart from the Pali-form term.

errors.why: The term is śakramūrdhan, the stock pramāṇa example of an anthill that emits smoke-like vapour; rendered literally without a note, it misleads.

note: A faithful rendering of a dense argument about fire, smoke and causal specificity.

errors.english: The nature of the quality of inherence does not have another quality called "form"
errors.why: ldan pa is saṃyoga (conjunction), which in Vaiśeṣika is a quality (guṇa), as the argument requires; 'inherence' (samavāya, 'du ba) is wrong here and throughout the side.

fix.find: The nature of the quality of inherence does not have another quality called "form"
fix.replace: Conjunction (saṃyoga), being of the nature of a quality, does not have another quality called "form"

note: The citra argument against the Vaiśeṣika is followed, but conjunction (saṃyoga) is consistently rendered as inherence, which confuses the categorial point.
